items.stem: The key difference between a budget and a forecast is that a budget:

options.text: Is a fixed plan and target, while a forecast is an updated expectation of the likely outcome
options.rationale: Correct: a budget is the plan; a forecast reflects the latest expected result.

options.text: Is always more accurate than a forecast
options.rationale: Forecasts, updated with actuals, are often closer to reality.

options.text: Is prepared after the year ends
options.rationale: Budgets are set before the period.

items.explanation: Correct: a budget is the plan; a forecast reflects the latest expected result.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO practices improve the usefulness of a budget? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Building it from measurable drivers and stated assumptions
options.rationale: Correct: driver-based budgets are transparent and testable.

options.text: Providing a sensitivity range around key assumptions
options.rationale: Correct: sensitivities show how outcomes change if assumptions move.

options.text: Copying last year and adding a flat percentage with no analysis
options.rationale: This ignores real drivers and change.

items.explanation: Correct: driver-based budgets are transparent and testable.
